SpaceX is putting supercomputers in orbit on Starship, starting next year.

Starmine satellites with onboard compute, powered by the sun, cooled by space, beaming data through Starlink lasers. Then the moon with Artemis, then Mars thousands of launches a year to build a self-sustaining city.

Two pads in Texas, three coming in Florida, and Starbase Louisiana on the way.

History in the making.

Flight 4 had a flap burning on reentry. After Flight 13, the ship floated in the ocean for weeks.

Flight 14 flies tomorrow, and it is the first Starship flight with reused heat shield tiles: two tiles from Ship 40 are flying again on Ship 41.

"The toughest remaining problem is a reusable orbital heat shield." @elonmusk

The window opens Mon, Sept 28 at 7:15 a.m. CT / 5:15 a.m. PT, pending regulatory approval.
